```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(data.table)
a  <- file.path(params$root, "analysis")
ld <- fread(file.path(a, "did_long_difference.csv"))
es <- fread(file.path(a, "did_event_study.csv"))
im <- fread(file.path(a, "did_implied_changes.csv"))
sz <- fread(file.path(a, "did_size_percentiles.csv"))
S  <- readRDS(file.path(a, "did_sample.rds"))
D  <- c("naive | recipient match", "proforma | recipient match", "proforma | combined match")
DL <- c("Recipient alone", "Pro forma, recipient match", "Pro forma, combined match")
OUT <- c(LOG_REVENUE = "Log revenue", LOG_ASSETS = "Log assets", MARGIN = "Operating margin",
         LOG_EXP_ASSETS = "Log(expenses / assets)", LOG_EMPLOYEES = "Log(1 + employees)")
star <- function(p) fcase(p < .01, "***", p < .05, "**", p < .1, "*", default = "")
pct <- function(b, y) ifelse(y == "MARGIN", sprintf("%+.1f pts", 100 * b), sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * (exp(b) - 1)))
cell <- function(b, se, p, y) sprintf("%s%s<br><small>%.3f (%.3f)</small>", pct(b, y), star(p), b, se)
wide <- function(x, label = "Group") {
  x <- copy(x)[, design := factor(design, D, DL)][, outcome := factor(outcome, names(OUT), OUT)]
  x[, v := cell(estimate, se, p, as.character(names(OUT))[as.integer(outcome)])]
  w <- dcast(x, outcome + term ~ design, value.var = "v")
  setnames(w, c("outcome", "term"), c("Outcome", label))
  w
}
kt <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, escape = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), ...)
n_sets <- function(dsg) ld[spec == "pooled" & design == dsg & outcome == "LOG_REVENUE", n_sets]
b_of <- function(dsg, y, spec = "pooled", term = "") ld[design == dsg & outcome == y & spec == !!spec & term == !!term, estimate]
```

How do nonprofits that absorb another organization through a merger fare
afterwards? This report estimates changes in revenue, assets,
profitability, spending relative to assets, and employment for recipients
in two-party mergers, compared with matched organizations that did not
merge. Matching and the sample are described in `matching-report.html`.

# Methods

## Two ways to define "better off"

Absorbing a donor adds its assets, revenue, and staff to the recipient's
books, so a recipient's size rises mechanically. That gives two
reasonable questions, which we estimate side by side:

* **Recipient alone.** *Did the recipient grow?* Before and after are both
  the recipient's own figures. This includes the absorbed donor, so it
  measures growth from the recipient's point of view.
* **Pro forma.** *Is the merged organization more than the sum of its
  parts?* "Before" adds the donor's figures to the recipient's, each on
  its own fiscal calendar. "After" is the recipient alone. A value of zero
  means the combined organization held onto everything the two had
  separately, relative to controls.

The pro forma version is estimated twice:

* with controls matched to the recipient alone (the original match);
* with controls re-matched to the combined size of recipient plus donor.

## Specification

**Long difference (headline).** For organization *i* in matched set *s*:

$$\Delta y_{is} = y_{is,t+2} - y_{is,t-2} = \alpha_s + \beta\, \text{Merger}_i + \varepsilon_{is}$$

* α~s~ is a fixed effect for each matched set: one recipient and its
  same-year controls. Because controls share the recipient's calendar
  year, α~s~ also absorbs year effects.
* Recipients have weight 1, and each control has weight 1/k within its
  set.
* Standard errors are clustered two ways, by matched set and by
  organization, because a control can appear in more than one set.
* Only sets with a recipient and at least one control observed in both
  years are used.

**Event study.** For years t-3 to t+2, with t-2 as the reference:

$$y_{ist} = \mu_{is} + \lambda_{s,t} + \sum_{k \neq -2} \beta_k\, \text{Merger}_i \cdot 1[t = k] + \varepsilon_{ist}$$

The coefficient at t-3 is the pre-trend test. t0 is a transition year
(partial-year books, assets arriving, one-time contribution revenue), so
we read results at t+1 and t+2.

**Heterogeneity.** The long difference is re-estimated with Merger
interacted with:

* the transfer size: fair market value transferred as a share of the
  recipient's assets at t-2;
* recipient size band;
* affiliation;
* CEO outcome;
* board outcome.

Each group's coefficient is its own effect relative to its own controls.

## Outcomes

| Outcome | Definition |
|---|---|
| Log revenue | log of total revenue, 2024 dollars |
| Log assets | log of total assets (end of year), 2024 dollars |
| Operating margin | (revenue − expenses) / revenue, bounded to −1..1 |
| Log(expenses / assets) | trimmed at the 1st and 99th percentiles |
| Log(1 + employees) | Part V employee count; full Form 990 filers only |

**Reading the coefficients.** Log coefficients are converted to percent
changes, exp(β) − 1, relative to controls over the same years. For
example, 0.244 is +27.7% and −0.062 is −6.0%. Margin coefficients are in
percentage points. Tables show the percent change with significance stars
(\*\*\* p < .01, \*\* p < .05, \* p < .1), and the log-point estimate with
its standard error underneath.

# Results

## Event study

![](`r file.path(a, "event_study.png")`)

```{r pretrend}
pt <- es[E == -3L, list(design = factor(design, D, DL), outcome = OUT[outcome], b = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", estimate, se))]
kt(dcast(pt, outcome ~ design, value.var = "b"), caption = "Pre-trend: coefficient at t-3 (reference t-2)")
```

There are no pre-trends: every t-3 coefficient is within 0.02 of zero. In
the recipient-alone version, revenue and assets begin to rise at t-1. That
is most likely fiscal years not lining up, or the merger beginning before
the donor's final return. After t0 the effects are flat through t+2.

## Main effects

```{r pooled}
kt(wide(ld[spec == "pooled"], "")[, !""], caption = sprintf(
  "Long difference t-2 to t+2. Matched sets: %s (recipient match), %s (combined match)",
  format(n_sets(D[1]), big.mark = ","), format(n_sets(D[3]), big.mark = ",")))
```

```{r implied}
iv <- im[, list(Design = factor(design, D, DL), Measure = measure, Change = sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * pct_change),
                p25 = fifelse(measure == "employees", sprintf("%+.0f", chg_p25), sprintf("%+.2fm", chg_p25 / 1e6)),
                Median = fifelse(measure == "employees", sprintf("%+.0f", chg_p50), sprintf("%+.2fm", chg_p50 / 1e6)),
                p75 = fifelse(measure == "employees", sprintf("%+.0f", chg_p75), sprintf("%+.2fm", chg_p75 / 1e6)))]
setorder(iv, Measure, Design)
szt <- sz[, list(Base = base, Measure = measure,
                 p25 = fifelse(measure == "employees", sprintf("%.0f", p25), sprintf("$%.1fm", p25 / 1e6)),
                 Median = fifelse(measure == "employees", sprintf("%.0f", p50), sprintf("$%.1fm", p50 / 1e6)),
                 p75 = fifelse(measure == "employees", sprintf("%.0f", p75), sprintf("$%.1fm", p75 / 1e6)))]
kt(szt, caption = "Baseline size of recipients and of recipient + donor combined")
kt(iv, caption = "Implied changes at those sizes (dollars in millions, 2024 dollars; employees in people). Recipient alone applies the change to the recipient's size; pro forma applies it to the combined size")
```

**Recipient alone.** Recipients grow substantially compared with similar
organizations that did not merge. Two years on, the median recipient has
about $2m more in assets, $1.1m more in revenue, and 6 more employees.
Most of this is the donor's books arriving: the growth rises steeply with
transfer size (below).

**Pro forma.** The merged organization ends up slightly smaller than the
two organizations were separately:

* assets about 4–6% smaller;
* revenue 7–9% smaller;
* staff about 8% smaller.

Roughly, 1 + 1 ≈ 1.9 after two years. Re-matching controls on the
combined size barely changes this, so the shortfall is not caused by
controls being the wrong size.

**Profitability does not change.** Operating margin is flat in every
version. It spikes at t0 (about +5 points) as the donated assets are
booked as one-time contribution revenue, then returns to zero.
Expenses-to-assets falls 2–3%, because assets grow more than spending.

## By transfer size

```{r dose}
kt(wide(ld[spec == "dose"][, term := sub("DOSE_BIN", "", term)], "Transfer / recipient assets"),
   caption = "Long difference by transfer size")
```

Recipient-alone growth tracks the size of the transfer. Assets grow about
4% when the transfer is under 1% of the recipient's assets, and about 145%
when it is half or more. The pro forma revenue shortfall appears in every
band, even the smallest. So donors were larger at t-2 than what they finally
handed over: they shrink before dissolving.

## By recipient size

```{r size}
kt(wide(ld[spec == "size"][, term := sub("SIZE_BAND", "", term)], "Recipient assets (baseline)"),
   caption = "Long difference by recipient size")
```

The largest recipients ($100m+ in assets) come closest to keeping the full
combined assets and revenue: their pro forma estimates are near zero, with
some loss of staff. Mid-size recipients ($10–100m) shed the most staff in
the pro forma comparison. Small recipients (under $10m) grow the most on
their own books and show the largest pro forma revenue loss.

## By affiliation

```{r aff}
kt(wide(ld[spec == "affiliated"][, term := fifelse(term == "AFFILIATEDTRUE", "Affiliated", "Arm's length")], "Pair"),
   caption = "Long difference by affiliation")
```

Mergers within one family of organizations show less recipient-alone
growth and larger pro forma losses. Part of that is mechanical: an
affiliated donor's revenue often includes grants from the parent or a
sister organization, so adding donor and recipient revenue counts some
money twice. Arm's-length mergers show a small margin gain in the
pro forma version with the recipient match.

## By CEO outcome

```{r ceo}
kt(wide(ld[spec == "ceo"][, term := sub("CEO_CAT", "", term)], "CEO outcome"),
   caption = "Long difference by CEO outcome (single-donor mergers with both CEOs identified)")
```

**Recipient keeps its CEO vs. both CEOs remain.** Recipient-alone growth
is similar in the two groups:

* revenue +26% when only the recipient's CEO remains, and +35% when both
  remain;
* assets +25% and +33%;
* employees +25% and +38%.

The point estimates are larger when both CEOs stay. That fits larger donors
whose operations and leaders both come across. But the two groups'
confidence intervals overlap, and only `r ld[design == D[1] & spec == "ceo" & term == "CEO_CATboth_ceos" & outcome == "LOG_REVENUE", n_sets]`
sets are estimated in total across all CEO groups.

In the pro forma comparison, mergers where only the recipient's CEO
remains are the closest to "1 + 1 = 2": assets and revenue are about
zero, and margin is +2.7 points with the recipient match. Mergers where
the two organizations already shared a CEO show the smallest
recipient-alone growth and the largest pro forma revenue loss, consistent
with affiliated deals.

## By board outcome

```{r board}
kt(wide(ld[spec == "board"][, term := sub("BOARD_CAT", "", term)], "Board outcome"),
   caption = "Long difference by board outcome")
```

* **The recipient's board stays intact and the donor's board dissolves.**
  This is the most common pattern. It has the smallest recipient-alone
  growth: revenue +13%, assets +17%, employees +8%. In the pro forma
  comparison it loses about 8% of revenue and 10% of staff. It looks like
  an absorption.
* **The boards combine (`combine_minor`, `combine_major`).** Recipient-alone
  growth is larger: assets +32% and +70%. With a minor share of donor
  seats, the merged organization holds onto its combined assets, revenue,
  and staff in the pro forma comparison (estimates near zero).
* **Donor members take 20% or more of the seats (`combine_major`).** These
  are mergers of near-equals. Margin falls about 5 points and pro forma
  revenue falls about 13–16%. Integration seems to be costlier.
* **The recipient's board turns over.** This shows large recipient-alone
  growth but pro forma losses similar to the intact-board group.

These governance categories are observed after the merger. They are
descriptive, not causal: a combined board may reflect a larger or more
equal deal, rather than produce a better outcome.

# Robustness: merger years through 2021

```{r rob-setup}
rb_dir <- file.path(a, "maxyear2021")
has_rb <- file.exists(file.path(rb_dir, "did_long_difference.csv"))
if (has_rb) {
  rb  <- fread(file.path(rb_dir, "did_long_difference.csv"))
  rbe <- fread(file.path(rb_dir, "did_event_study.csv"))
  rbf <- fread(file.path(rb_dir, "did_funnel.csv"))
  n_rb <- rbf[grepl("same-year control \\(recipient", step), n]
  n_rb_c <- rbf[grepl("same-year control \\(combined", step), n]
}
cmp <- function(spec_, label = NULL) {
  x <- rbind(ld[spec == spec_][, run := "All years"], rb[spec == spec_][, run := "Through 2021"])
  x[, design := factor(design, D, DL)][, y := outcome][, outcome := factor(outcome, names(OUT), OUT)]
  x[, v := sprintf("%s%s", pct(estimate, y), star(p))]
  if (!is.null(label)) x[, term := sub(label, "", term)]
  w <- dcast(x, outcome + term ~ design + run, value.var = "v", sep = ": ")
  if (all(w$term == "")) w[, term := NULL]
  setnames(w, intersect(c("outcome", "term"), names(w)), c("Outcome", "Group")[seq_along(intersect(c("outcome", "term"), names(w)))])
  w
}
```

`r if (!has_rb) "*Robustness results not found: run did-recipients.R with MAX_YEAR=2021 and OUT_SUBDIR=maxyear2021.*"`

```{r rob, eval = has_rb, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "Mergers in 2022 and 2023 have post-periods that run into 2024 and 2025, and 2025 is only partly",
  "filed. Calendar-year effects on the t-2 to t+2 change are jointly significant for every outcome,",
  "and margins are lower in windows ending in 2024 and 2025. This check re-runs every model with",
  "merger years 2011 to 2021 only: %s recipients in the recipient match (%s in the combined match),",
  "compared with %s and %s in the main sample.\n\n"),
  format(n_rb, big.mark = ","), format(n_rb_c, big.mark = ","),
  format(n_sets(D[1]), big.mark = ","), format(n_sets(D[3]), big.mark = ",")))
```

```{r rob-pooled, eval = has_rb}
kt(cmp("pooled"), caption = "Main effects: all merger years vs. merger years through 2021 (percent change, or percentage points for margin)")
```

```{r rob-gov, eval = has_rb}
kt(cmp("ceo", "CEO_CAT")[Outcome %in% c("Log revenue", "Log assets", "Operating margin")],
   caption = "CEO outcome splits, all years vs. through 2021")
kt(cmp("board", "BOARD_CAT")[Outcome %in% c("Log revenue", "Log assets", "Operating margin")],
   caption = "Board outcome splits, all years vs. through 2021")
```

```{r rob-event, eval = has_rb}
ev <- rbind(es[, run := "All years"], rbe[, run := "Through 2021"])[outcome == "MARGIN"]
ev[, design := factor(design, D, DL)]
kt(dcast(ev, design + run ~ E, value.var = "estimate", fun.aggregate = function(v) round(v, 3)),
   caption = "Event study for operating margin (reference t-2)")
```

`r if (has_rb) "**The results do not depend on the latest merger years.** Every main-effect estimate moves by less than 1.5 log points, and the signs and significance are unchanged. Without 2022–2023, margin estimates rise slightly (about +0.5 to +0.7 points), so the incomplete 2024–2025 returns were pulling margins down a little, but the pooled margin effect is still zero. The margin event study looks the same: a one-time spike at t0 and a return to zero by t+1. The governance splits also hold. The margin gain when only the recipient's CEO remains gets stronger (about +5 points in the pro forma comparison with the recipient match), and the margin decline when donor members hold 20% or more of the recipient's board seats is unchanged at about −5 points."`

# Interpretation and caveats

* **Both versions are informative.** From the recipient's point of view,
  mergers are growth: substantial, lasting, and with no loss of operating
  margin. From the combined point of view, the merged organization
  keeps about 92–95% of the two organizations' joint revenue and assets
  after two years, with about 8% fewer staff. Neither is "the" answer. The
  recipient-alone version overstates the gain, and the pro forma version
  likely overstates the loss.
* **The pro forma version is a lower bound.** It assumes the donor would
  have kept its full t-2 size, but dissolving organizations were usually
  shrinking already. For affiliated pairs, adding donor and recipient
  revenue can count intra-family grants twice. A tighter version would
  use the donor at t-1, or scale the donor's figures by the share of its
  assets actually transferred.
* **Survival.** Recipients and controls must both file through t+2, so the
  results describe organizations that survive. About 98% of recipients
  keep filing.
* **Employment** is observed only for full Form 990 filers. 990-EZ donors
  count as zero employees in the pro forma.
* **Matching** controls for observed size, sector, year, and margin. It
  cannot rule out that organizations chosen as merger partners were on
  different paths for unobserved reasons. The flat pre-trends help, but
  they do not prove the absence of such differences.
